plausibility_notes: Every attendee now confesses a scandal and an antagonistic interaction with Grant. Motives spread broadly; Monet faces imminent audit, Hugh unaffordable refund and accusation, Barb has misconduct and suppression. None of these establishes murder.
Artie alternate job weakens dismissal motive but cannot exonerate; the job is self-reported and forgery remains serious. Threat withdrawal or victim hypocrisy never proves innocence.
Dada explains threat as artistic grievance and Minnie explains blackout as sabotage, but these admissions do not exclude poisoning. Need independent evidence for timing and method.
Vincent explicitly contemplated larger revenge. Brie has service access and payment disputes. Claire and Anya provenance suppression gives existential institutional motive.

Thirty speeches share the same confession-qualification-victim-pressure structure and very articulate self-awareness. Occupational details distinguish them more than rhythm or psychology; confession parade feels administratively arranged.
